Hi guys,

Sorry, but I discovered this subverse a couple of days ago and I've been really glad that I've been able to comment. As many people mentioned about r/TwoXChromosomes people were being downvoted for the most innocuous comments, which made it a pretty hostile place to contribute to.

This place on the other hand is relatively new, so discussion is still open. There is also one mod who doesn't seem to be active. A couple of awesome users are posting a variety of links which is really nice.

However, perhaps one of the drawbacks is that there is a bit of an SJW backlash that fringes on a backlash against women and I see people coming in here and complaining about that.

I think a few troll comments is the small price we pay to be able to voice our opinions without being downvoated or brigaded for some seemingly-innocuous detail.

I also think we should all reflect upon why this backlash has come about and possibly take a little responsibility. We know that many feminist subreddits became very toxic, leading to people leaving to this site, including myself and some other people on this subreddit.

We also know that censorship and insisting that some views that we don't agree with be removed escalated into something worse at Reddit. So as much as I don't like the anti-women comments here and there, I tolerate it. Because a) I don't think anyone is really convinced by them and b) More reasonable comments will drown out the negativity.

Lastly I think that if we don't even care enough to contribute in a relatively safe environment (none of the trolls have responded to me) to drown out those negative statements, and worse if we somehow believe that silencing those statements just because somehow makes them go away and not fester in resentment, maybe this project isn't really worth it.

We've got a great opportunity to start a place where all women can come forward and tell us what they really think without being in a hostile environment.
